counterexamples.boundary: Prior-round findings remain valid historical evidence when explicitly labeled superseded and are not an active instruction.
A single authority may legitimately have generated or read-only consumers; the defect is duplicate normative ownership, not repeated textual references.

findings.summary: P0 retains duplicate and conflicting affected-l2 instructions, including a forbidden registry-pruning remedy.
R-28, P8, and completion text retain stale RM2/ledger closure semantics after canonical transfer and 7+1 decisions.
P3-B/P3-D boundary does not yet make the nonvisual adapter, logical command identity, and unknown-result terminal state unambiguous.
The planned typed blocker information lacks a named closed contract field and a generated transport-preservation chain.
Blocker-store disclosure must not expose identifiers outside the acting user's visible scope.
Receipt replay and the P3-D command-count assertion must distinguish immutable action acknowledgement from fresh owner readback and same-key recovery retries.
